Theorem
[Blow-up for large initial data] ↗ def:principal-eigenvalue 1. ch9:9.4.1-thm-1\group Nonexistence

Let $u$ be a smooth solution of (1) with $g\geq 0$, $g\not\equiv 0$, let $w_1$ satisfy (3), and define $\eta (t)=\int _Uu(x,t)w_1(x)\, dx$. If \[ \eta (0) = \int _U gw_1 \, dx > \lambda _1, \] set \[ t^*:=-\frac1{\lambda _1}\log \left(\frac{\eta (0)-\lambda _1}{\eta (0)}\right). \tag {10} \] Then either smoothness fails before $t^*$ or \[ \lim _{t \to t_*} \int _U u(x,t)w_1(x) \, dx = \infty \] for some $0<t_*\leq t^*$. In particular, no smooth solution exists on every interval $[0,T]$ with $T\geq t^*$.

Proof

\sketch Set $\xi (t)=e^{\lambda _1t}\eta (t)$. Inequality (6) gives $\dot\xi \geq e^{-\lambda _1t}\xi ^2$, whose integrated reciprocal inequality has a denominator vanishing at $t^*$. Thus $\eta $ becomes unbounded no later than $t^*$ unless the assumed smooth solution ceases to exist first.

□
